#791. Khloe Kardashian Is "Down" for Lavender Marriage Amid Celibacy

Khloe Kardashian admitted she’s thought about entering a lavender marriage after years of celibacy on the Nov. 26 episode of The Kardashians: "It depends what that gay man can do for me."

Khloe Kardashian is weighing in on the possibility of tying the knot again—but not in the traditional sense.

The Khloe in Wonderland host—who has been single and celibate since her 2021 breakup from Tristan Thompson—revealed whether she’d be open to a lavender marriage in the future.

“You need a man, all your sisters are dating,” content creator Colt Paulsen told Khloe on the Nov. 26 episode of The Kardashians. “You can always do the lavender marriage. If you ever need, I’m here.”

“Oh yeah, well, that?” Khloe responded. “I’m down with anytime.”

The Hulu series shared the definition of a lavender marriage onscreen, describing the bond as “a marriage of convenience between a man and a woman where one or both partners is queer.”

And though Khloe—mom to daughter True, 8, and son Tatum, 4, with Tristan—initially expressed that she would be into the unconventional relationship, she later admitted that she does have some hesitations.

“Would I have a lavender marriage? There’s times, yes, and then other times, I’m like, to take care of one more person? I don’t know,” she explained in a confessional. “I mean, it depends what that gay man can do for me.”

“Will you make me look pretty every day? Sold,” she quipped. “That’s all it takes.”

While time will tell whether Khloe will embark on a lavender marriage in her future, she recently shared insight into her sexuality after her longtime friend Simon Huck suggested that the Revenge Body alum falls into the category of a demisexual.

“A demisexual is a person who can only be romantic and intimate with someone if they’ve first established an emotional relationship,” he shared on the Nov. 18 episode of Khloe’s Khloe in Wonder Land podcast. “So, it’s almost impossible to have a one-night stand if you’re a demi. And I believe you are also a demi.”

Khloe admitted that she felt the term is quite fitting. After all, she mused, “I don’t think I’ve ever had a one-night stand. I would remember. I’m a demi? Wow.”

And though the mom of two noted that she isn’t in the right “headspace” to “lean into someone” at the moment, she does often miss physical intimacy.

“I just want to be kissed sometimes,” Khloe shared. “But not necessarily, 'I just need to have sex.' Sometimes I just miss a normal nice hug—but from someone you want that hug from.”

To keep up with the latest on the love lives of Khloe and her family, read on…

Why, yes, Kris Jenner and longtime love Corey Gamble are still doing amazing, sweetie. In 2014, the music industry insider approached the world's most famous momager at fashion designer Riccardo Tisci's 40th birthday bash in Ibiza and "I just tried saying, 'You're beautiful. I'd love to get to know you,'" he shared on the family's OG series, Keeping Up With the Kardashians, "and it went from there."

More than a decade in, Kris gushed about her "ride or die" in a 2025 birthday tribute, writing, "Thank you for all you do every single day, for the love you give, and for always being there for all of us. I’m so blessed to have you by my side."

With all due respect for all the small things, Kourtney Kardashian's husband has made some pretty grand gestures throughout their yearlong marriage. Take her 44th birthday that saw her and Travis Barker take a trip up the California coast to Santa Barbara. The Blink-182 drummer marked the occasion by filling their room at the famed Kennedy Cottage with rose petals and gifting her with a $161,819 piece by artist Yoshitomo Nara. The Poosh founder has fully embraced her new life as the girl at the rock show. And in November 2023, she and Travis welcomed their first child together, son Rocky Thirteen Barker.

As Kim Kardashian put it in The Kardashians trailer, "Things change really quickly." When season two wrapped, the SKIMS founder was still with then-Saturday Night Live standout Pete Davidson.

She got fans hoping she was getting back in the dating game with retired NFL quarterback Tom Brady.

Alas, the mom to North West, Saint West, Chicago West and Psalm West—with ex-husband Kanye West—wasn't on the hunt for a new teammate, a source telling E! News in May 2023, "They have friends and business partners in common."

By early 2026, she was racing into a new romance with Lewis Hamilton, hard-launching her relationship with the F1 driver that June.

In a 2023 episode, Kris shoots her shot while chatting with Khloe Kardashian about Tristan Thompson, asking, "How's everything going with Tristan?" Safe to say the Good American founder has the basketball player benched for now. Though the exes have worked out a game plan for raising daughter True and son Tatum, Khloe shot down the idea that they're back together in May 2023, calling the narrative "tiring."

She's more interested in starting a fresh story. After meeting Love Is Blind star Alexa Lemieux the following April, Khloe pitched a winning idea to Netflix, writing on Instagram, "I think some of us single K sisters should go on LIB. What do you think?"

Months after Kendall Jenner's split with NBA guard Devin Booker in fall 2022, the model's love life got an assist from friends Justin Bieber and Hailey Bieber. The married duo were spotted enjoying a double date with the reality star and musician Bad Bunny in February 2023. The following December, it was reported that the two had called it quits.

Then in the spring of 2026, fans started to wonder if a new romance was in bloom as Kendall was spotted hanging out with Jacob Elordi. The Euphoria alum was among those cheering for the model when she walked in Milan Fashion Week in September 2026.

Seems Kylie Jenner has found herself a new beautiful boy. Last seen publicly with rapper Travis Scott—dad to her daughter Stormi and son Aire—at an Art Basel party in December 2022, the beauty mogul, has first linked to Oscar-nominated actor Timothée Chalamet in April 2023.

Now, rise and shine because you don't want to miss the glimpses they've given us of their romance at New York Fashion Week and the US Open, as well as live on TV, when they showed PDA while seated together at the 2024 Golden Globes and 2025 Oscars.

Then, while accepting Best Actor at the 2026 Critics Choice Awards in January, he thanked his "partner of three years," for the foundation she provides, adding, "I couldn't do this without you. Thank you from the bottom of my heart."

#790. Measles in America: Here's a constructive approach to beating the disease, based on Brazil's experience

The US is now officially a measles contagion zone. By mid-2026, there were more infections than in all of the previous year. But the country could beat measles again, just like Brazil did two years ago.

Health experts saw it coming — the fact that after 26 years, the US would lose its status as measles-free. Back in July 2026, DW reported how one epidemiologist had suggested an 'amnesia' about the measles risk was pushing a growth in US infections.

Four months later, it was official. On November 17, 2026, the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) said the US had lost its measles elimination status, along with Mexico.

Look at Brazil, where in 2019, with more than 21,000 measles cases, the country also lost its measles-free status. But within five years — during the COVID-19 pandemic — it fought and won back its measles-free status. And since 2024, Brazil has stayed measles-free, even as the highly contagious disease spread across the rest of the Americas.

In 2026, with the data available up to the time of writing this article, Brazil had only had 70 measles cases. They were all linked to infections brought in from abroad, often from neighboring Peru.

Brazil has fewer people than the US, about 213 million compared to the US's nearly 350 million, but the two countries are similar in size. So the comparison is worth considering.

Brazil moves fast. The PAHO asks countries to respond within 72 hours of a suspected measles case. Here's Brazil's own rule:

It has also made hunting for cases a national habit. In a program called "Dia S," health workers knock on doors and visit schools, daycare centers and churches to find people who may be sick but have not seen a doctor.

Brazil also holds mass vaccination days called "Dia D." There was one in November, in the area where Brazil borders Colombia and Peru.

If someone is diagnosed with measles, health workers try to track down every person the patient may have met ("contact persons") and vaccinate them and other people living nearby.

The country has so far provided more than 16 million doses of the measles vaccine in 2026 and has donated 500,000 doses to Peru.

Brazil isn't perfect, though. According to official estimates from the World Health Organization, only 76% of children got both required doses of the vaccine in 2025 — well short of the 95% target. Experts warn this leaves the country at risk because measles is so highly contagious. A country needs to be as close to 100% immunized as possible to protect people and stop the disease from spreading.

"Elimination is not a trophy that we win once and put on a shelf. It must be protected every day," says PAHO Director Jarbas Barbosa.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

The US lost its measles-free status because the PAHO found that the same strain of the virus had been spreading in the country for 12 months or more. Mexico and Bolivia lost their status on the same day as the US.

The US has had more than 5,400 cases in 2026 (at time of writing), more than twice as many as in all of 2025, and about 19 times as many as in 2024. Nearly everyone who got sick with measles was unvaccinated or had an unknown vaccination status.

US President Donald Trump signed an executive order on new vaccination recommendations for children in August 2026. It came at a time, when, as we reported, experts said people had stopped getting vaccinated against measles because infection rates were low. But like PAHO's Barbosa said, neglecting vaccination when infection rates are low is a mistake.

To be fair, Trump's executive order listed the measles vaccine in a top category of vaccinations recommended for every child. But the administration's stance on vaccination in general is unclear.

Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. has often declared opposition to vaccination, including against measles, advising people to take vitamin A instead. In Texas, this led to children being hospitalized with toxic levels of the supplement, and left them with no protection against measles.

Before the COVID-19 pandemic, 95% of US kindergartners had their measles shots. Now, it's 92%, according to the US Centers for Disease Control and Protection (CDC). That leaves about 280,000 kindergartners in the US unprotected.

In the Texas counties where a 2025 measles outbreak began, coverage was as low as 77% at the time.

US children usually need vaccines to start school, but most states let parents opt out for religious or personal reasons, with no doctor involved.

But vaccination rates have fallen elsewhere in the world as well, including in Europe. In Germany, where measles infections have also risen, experts blame anti-vaccination rhetoric that emerged during the COVID-19 pandemic.

A person sick with measles can infect up to18 other, unprotected people. With vaccination, it is possible to increase the number of protected people and lower the number of people the sick person can infect.

To prevent a measles outbreak, a community needs about 95% of people to be vaccinated and/or immune. The vaccination consists of two doses of the MMR (measles, mumps, rubella) vaccine.

But even after the two doses, a person can expect to have only 97% protection against measles — 3% short of full protection — so, nearly everyone in the community has to be vaccinated to keep the average level of protect as close to 100% as possible.

"For some diseases like measles, even a small decrease in vaccination rates can lead to more outbreaks of disease [so] community immunity requires over 95% of susceptible individuals to be immunized," says Andrew Racine, president of the American Academy of Pediatrics.

And the 95% has to hold everywhere. A good national average can be affected by, for example, a single school where only 70% of the children are vaccinated. And that is where the outbreak is likely to start.

Around the world, measles deaths have dropped by 88% since 2000, thanks to vaccines.

But progress has stalled. Only about three out of four children worldwide get both doses of the vaccine. The biggest outbreaks right now are in Bangladesh, Indonesia and Guatemala.

Data from Europe shows that things can get better. In the European Union, cases fell from more than 35,000 in 2024 to about 2,300 the following year, with no measles-related deaths.

Romania went from more than 30,000 cases in 2024 to about 4,200 in 2025.

In Hungary, where 99% of children are vaccinated, there have been no measles cases in the past year.

But in January, six European countries lost their measles-free status, including the UK, Spain and Austria. Across Europe, eight out of ten people who got measles in 2025 were unvaccinated.

The Americas are seeing a major surge in measles infections, with more than 58,000 cases in 2026, over four times as many as by November in 2025. Guatemala has been hit hardest, with almost 35,000 cases.

The deadliest outbreaks are in Africa. African Union countries have so far reported nearly 1,800 measles deaths in 2026, about 1,650 of them in Democratic Republic of Congo. Yet, Sudan, despite the war, raised first-dose measles coverage by 22 percentage points in 2025, which was the world's largest gain.

Measles is extremely contagious. One person can infect up to 18 unprotected people, which makes it about 12 times more contagious than the flu.

The virus can linger in the air for up to two hours after a sick person has left the room. And people spread it before they know they are sick. Someone with measles is contagious for four days before the rash appears and four days after.

It's not just a rash. About one in five unvaccinated people who get measles in the US ends up in the hospital. Measles can weaken the immune system for years, making it harder to fight off other infections.

But it's preventable. Two doses of the MMR vaccine (which also protects against mumps and rubella) protect 97% of people for life.

#788. Wales and West Ham's Morgan suffers serious injury

Ffion Morgan joined West Ham from Bristol City in 2025

Wales and West Ham winger Ffion Morgan is facing a lengthy spell on the sidelines after suffering an anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injury.

Morgan has undergone surgery having been helped off during West Ham's Women's Super League win over Charlton earlier this month.

The 26-year-old is now likely to miss the rest of the season.

"Ffion will now begin her rehabilitation programme under the supervision of the club's medical team," a West Ham statement said.

The injury also makes Morgan a major doubt for next summer's Women's World Cup, should Wales qualify.

Rhian Wilkinson's side take on Norway in a two-legged play-off final next week as they bid to reach the tournament for the first time in the nation's history.

Morgan, who has 56 caps, is an international regular and would be a shoo-in for the Wales squad if fit.

Five return for Wales' World Cup play-off final

Home World Cup can inspire Wales' future stars

She joined West Ham on a two-year deal in 2025 after her contract at Bristol City expired.

Morgan has also played for Cardiff City, Coventry United and Crystal Palace.

She suffered an ACL injury while playing for Wales Under-19s as a teenager, while she had only recently returned to action for West Ham after another lengthy fitness lay-off.

Wales face Norway at the Cardiff City Stadium on Tuesday, 1 December, before the return leg in Oslo four days later.

Wales are hoping to cause an upset as they bid to reach the Women's World Cup for the first time, though beating former champions Norway may not be enough to guarantee a place in Brazil next summer.

The complex nature of the qualification process means that Wales may have to negotiate inter-confederation play-offs next February to secure a World Cup place, even if they triumph over Norway.

#787. What will returning Magill bring to Northern Ireland?

Simone Magill made her return to football as a late substitute for Birmingham City against Manchester United on Sunday

After 13 months away, Simone Magill made her return to football as a late substitute in Birmingham City's WSL defeat by Manchester United on Sunday.

It was a moment that had been a long time coming for the 31-year-old, who gave birth to her daughter, Skye, in May and has been building towards stepping back on the pitch.

Now, she will hope to make her international return with Northern Ireland in a friendly against Greece on Friday.

"It's been some time since I've been here in a playing capacity, so it's really nice just to be back in the mix again," NI captain Magill told BBC Sport NI.

"I officially made my comeback at the weekend and it was really nice to have done that. I'm really looking forward to doing that here at home in front of the fans and my family as well."

'You can be a mum and a footballer - they can co-exist'

Greece friendlies an opportunity to build - Andrews

In an interview with BBC Sport in October, Magill spoke about how being both a mum and a footballer can "co-exist".

While she was not ready to play any role in the matches, Magill, Skye and her husband Mark were all in camp for the World Cup play-off with Portugal last month, all with an eye of integrating into international duty as a family.

Having played just a handful of minutes, Northern Ireland manager Michael McArdle said that while he was "delighted" to have Magill back, how much she plays across the double-header would be in collaboration with Birmingham and his captain.

"With the circumstances around this one, I'm very mindful that I need to build accordingly and I really need to listen to myself as well," Magill added.

"To even be back in this capacity this soon after giving birth, for me, is just unbelievable.

"I have no major expectations. I'm just really happy to be here and be a part of it, and if I do come on, that'll be even better."

Watch live on BBC iPlayer and the BBC Sport app and website

Friday's match against Greece will be Northern Ireland's first friendly in three years.

The sides will then play again on Tuesday at 16:00 GMT, and both matches can be streamed live on BBC iPlayer and the BBC Sport app and website.

The matches will act as preparation for the Nations League campaign in February, when Northern Ireland face tricky tests in the form of Poland, Finland and Belarus.

McArdle is developing a young squad and Magill says she hopes to bring "leadership and experience to really help us all move forward".

"We've obviously had a transition in the last year whilst I've been out, it's been nice to come back in and just feel where we're at, get on the grass with the girls and see, 'how can I help, what can I bring?'," she added.

"I'm very much looking forward to just getting back in the mix and helping try to bring the young players forward, use that experience and let's hold on to the ball, let's get into the final third, let's have a go, be brave - all of the attributes that we're known for.

"We're an underdog nation, so it's getting that across to the younger members in the squad to say, 'let's have a go with these teams and not be afraid'."

Simone Magill (centre) is set to make her Northern Ireland return against Greece

In her absence over the past year, Northern Ireland have used a number of different options in the centre forward role.

Winger Lauren Wade has shown her versatility by playing centrally, while Kess Elmore and Cora Chambers have also played up top.

Along with Magill, Portsmouth striker Kerry Beattie is also back in the squad to bolster McArdle's striking options.

"We've loads of young ones snapping at my heels. It's great, that's what we want.

"I feel we're more competitive now than ever. You never know who's going to be coming into the squad. Certainly, in more recent years, you kind of knew the squad every single time, whereas that's not the case now.

"We've got some exciting youth coming through, so it's their time now to shine."

Magill added that Northern Ireland are "heading in a new direction" ahead of the Nations League campaign next year, and the friendlies with Greece give an opportunity for the team to grow in a pressure-free environment.

"We're coming into a brand new campaign and it's really nice that we have a friendly window just now.

"We haven't had one in a very, very long time, so this is a brilliant opportunity to get us all back together, get the new faces in, get some more experience, learn things, try things.

"I'm really excited about where we're going."

#786. Germany's Freigang given 16-month ban over drugs test issues

Laura Freigang has scored 17 goals in 45 appearances for Germany

Germany international Laura Freigang has been suspended from football for 16 months over issues with three drugs tests.

The 28-year-old will miss the Women's World Cup next summer and is banned from all football activity until after 7 October 2027.

The 16-month suspension begins from the date of notification by the German Football Association (DFB), which took place in June.

The World Anti-Doping Agency (Wada), the National Anti-Doping Agency (Nada), DFB and Freigang reached a dispute resolution agreement.

The dispute said Entracht Frankfurt forward Freigang committed three reporting and/or testing failures between 11 March 2025 and 23 February 2026.

Freigang can return to training two months prior to the end of the suspension period but cannot play matches until after 7 October.

All personal records of appearances, goals, assists or other statistics from 23 February 2026 are nullified, though Frankfurt's results are unaffected.

This season Freigang has scored six goals and provided two assists in 11 starts in the Frauen-Bundesliga.

Since joining the club in 2020, the striker has scored 107 goals in 187 appearances and was in the Germany squad for October's friendly victories over Australia and Japan.

In a club statement, external, Franfurt said they will "begin discussions shortly to determine the terms of her future employment relationship".

Freigang's current contract is due to expire on 30 June 2027.

Frankfurt's director of women's football Katharina Kiel said: "The agreement now reached provides clarity and planning security in a process unprecedented for Eintracht Frankfurt - for us as a club, but above all for Laura.

"The way she and the team have handled the situation in recent months, and how Laura personally led by example with her performance on the pitch during a very difficult time, deserves the highest recognition.

"The identified shortcomings, despite the agreement to settle the dispute, have resulted in a suspension, which means the loss of a key player."

#785. How Jennifer Lopez and More Stars Are Celebrating Thanksgiving 2026

Thanksgiving 2026 is finally upon us, and Hollywood’s biggest stars are eager to kick back and relax this Turkey Day. From Hoda Kotb to Jennifer Lopez, see what they got up to.

It’s time to get basted—because Thanksgiving 2026 is officially here.

And with the most gratitude-filled day of the year comes a slew of stars ready to stop, drop and pass the dinner rolls with their loved ones. As for how they’ll be celebrating Turkey Day this time around?

Well, Lena Dunham offered a sweet glimpse into her first Thanksgiving as a mother, sharing a photo of her and husband Luis Felber's baby girl as they went on a family stroll.

As she captioned the Nov. 26 Instagram post, "Thankful."

Meanwhile, Jennifer Lopez revealed that while her and Marc Anthony’s 18-year-old twins Max and Emme are enjoying their first semester of college, they’ll be making their way back to Jenny’s block for the holiday season.

“I told them, I said, 'I don't care what you do,’” the singer told Drew Barrymore on the Nov. 23 episode of her eponymous talk show. “‘I know you're going to have friends. I know you're going to fall in love. I know you're going to do all the things. Thanksgiving and Christmas, I don't care if you bring 20 people, just come home. Please, just come home.’”

But it’s safe to say that their sweet reunion won’t make for your average Thanksgiving gathering. After all, the whole fam will be getting loud for the 57-year-old’s The JLO Show concert film, which premieres on CBS and Paramount+ on Nov. 26 at 8 p.m. ET.

“For me, as an entertainer, my job is to make sure everybody enjoys themselves and has a good time,” the “Jenny from the Block” the singer told E! News in an interview published Nov. 20. “Everything about the show is put together to tell a story.”

Barrymore, on the other hand, is sticking to her newfound blend of Thanksgiving traditions.

“I didn't have them growing up, and I bet there are a lot of people out there who probably had that same kind of experience,” she told CBS Nov. 23. “And the good news is, you can find them and build them because now in my life, rich traditions.”

As for a few of the 50 first traditions she’s put in place?

“I really love decorating our door with like turkey hand puppets, and we have a whole box of Thanksgiving decorations, and we go out and get some gourds,” she explained. “We go to this pumpkin patch every year.”

“Growing up in West Hollywood, Los Angeles, there's no pumpkin patches around, and so the fact that I get to do that with my kids, I never thought that would be my life, and it is,” she added. “So even if your life didn't start that way, it can totally get there. And now I look forward to that pumpkin patch every year.”

Then there are some holiday traditions with deep roots. After all, this year’s Thanksgiving marks Macy’s 100th Thanksgiving Day Parade, which is hosted by none other than Savannah Guthrie, Hoda Kotb and Al Roker.

And while this year's event has been postponed to Nov. 28 due to severe weather, the Joy 101 founder made it clear there will be no rain on her parade.

“It’s OK,” Kotb said on the November 25 episode of Late Night With Seth Meyers. “We waited 100 years for this parade, we’re gonna wait two more days. We’re gonna have it on Saturday. It’s gonna be a beautiful, sunsplash day.”

In the meantime, she'll be spending the holiday watching last year's parade, which NBC announced would run as a place holder on Thanksgiving Day. As she put it, “We’re gonna watch an old parade and you won’t know the difference, OK? It’s gonna be spectacular.”

Keep reading to see how more stars are celebrating Thanksgiving 2026…

The “Honey Bee” singer and “Hollaback Girl” hitmaker snuggled in close as they expressed gratitude for their fans. As Shelton wrote on Instagram Nov. 26, “Hoping everybody has a happy Thanksgiving!!! Thankful for y'all!!!!”

The supermodel and jiu jitsu instructor showed off their model life with their 21-month-old son.

“The amount of goodness we experience in life depends on our ability to notice it," Bündchen captioned her Nov. 26 Instagram post, which also featured pictures of her and ex-husband Tom Brady's kids Benjamin, 16, and Vivian, 13. "Gratitude is contagious, and the more we can appreciate the beauty around us, the more joy we bring into our lives and the lives of others."

She added, "May we always find something to be grateful for, not just today, but every day. Happy Thanksgiving! Sending you all so much love."

It was a celebration for the girls as Dunham marked her first Thanksgiving as a mom alongside husband Luis Felber.

As she captioned the Nov. 26 Instagram post as the family went on a stroll, "Thankful."

You oughta know how excited the country music star is about the holiday season.

“Time for a little more peace, love and cowboys,” she wrote on Instagram Nov. 26. “Let the holiday shenanigans begin happy Thanksgiving from my family to y’all’s!”

The Freaky Friday star got reflective this Thanksgiving as she shared an image of herself stretching while enjoying an ocean view.

"Going to turn off the noise for a moment," she wrote on Instagram Nov. 26. "To all out there in this vast environment that we opt into, that if you're lucky enough to have one, the Thanksgiving meal is not hard. It's a roasted bird and potatoes."

"What's hard are the people with their binary and rigid ideas and judgments and petty selfishness," she added. "Today let's all be like Dolly [Parton] and be welcoming and gentle and generous."

The Red Table Talk host showed off her family's extravagant Thanksgiving set-up.

"Preparing for Thanksgiving dinner at the family abode," she wrote on Instagram Nov. 26. "Happy Day of thanks to you all and may you, your families and loved ones continue to be lifted and showered by the gifts of grace from the Highest. They may not always show up how we want them to … but they are there."

#784. Ipswich Women sign Ademiluyi for record fee

Ademiluyi had been on loan at the Tractor Girls from NWSL side Gotham FC since February

Ipswich Town Women have confirmed the permanent signing of England youth international Princess Ademiluyi for an undisclosed club record fee.

The 20-year-old forward has been on loan at the Tractor Girls from NWSL side Gotham FC since February and has agreed a three-and-a-half year deal at the WSL2 side.

Ademiluyi has been capped by England at under-19 and under-20 level, and has been called up for the under-23 side for the first time ahead of their internationals against Belgium and Portugal next week., external

"I have really made a home for myself in Suffolk and I am so excited to continue building what has been a positive start to the season for us as a group," she told the club's website., external

"The players, staff and supporters have all been brilliant with me since I arrived and I can't wait to see where this club can go and to continue making more memories together."

Ipswich Town chairman Mark Ashton said: "Signing Princess on a permanent basis has been a real priority for us and completing such a significant deal as this highlights the club's ongoing commitment to reach the top level of the game.

"This is a statement signing for the club, with further announcements to come in due course as we reaffirm our commitment to our women's set-up in both the short and long-term."

Ademiluyi started her career at WSL side West Ham in 2023 before moving to US-based Gotham and is Ipswich's top scorer so far in 2026-27, with four goals.

The Tractor Girls finished ninth in WSL2 last season following promotion to the second tier in 2025, and were in the fourth tier as recently as 2021., external

Under the management of former men's team player David Wright, appointed to the role in April, the Blues are third after eight games this season, three points behind leaders Newcastle United.

Ipswich on 'inevitable' path to WSL - Boswell

Ademiluyi has played an important role in helping the Tractor Girls transform from relegation candidates to title contenders.

She made an immediate impact on joining in February, scoring goals against Durham and Birmingham City to help secure the team's survival in WSL2.

The forward has continued to find the net this season, and won the WSL2 player of the month award for October., external

There is a growing feeling within the women's game that the Blues will be playing at the highest level in the not too distant future and securing a proven goalscorer whose stock is also rising on the international stage will only strengthen that train of thought.

#783. Sean “Diddy” Combs’ Prison Thanksgiving Meal Revealed

Sean “Diddy” Combs is spending his third Thanksgiving behind bars this year, and his Turkey Day meal is set to include all the fixings.

Sean “Diddy” Combs isn’t skipping out on Turkey Day.

After all, the rapper—who is serving a 50-month prison sentence for prostitution related charges at FCI Allenwood Low in Pennsylvania—will enjoy a full-course meal come Nov. 26, a law enforcement official at the prison confirmed to People.

Combs' Thanksgiving menu includes a choice between turkey and tofu stir-fry, they told the outlet, along with sides like mashed potatoes and candied sweet potato casserole.

And it appears the music mogul will be able to enjoy all the fixings as the menu also features green bean casserole, sage and onion stuffing and dinner rolls, the official confirmed. Combs will also have his choice of gravy and cranberry sauce for the meal.

And what’s Thanksgiving without dessert? This year, the 57-year-old will satisfy his sweet tooth with pecan pie.

E! News has reached out to Combs’ rep for comment but did not hear back.

But not every inmate will be getting the same spread. In fact, the Federal Bureau of Prisons (BOP) does not offer a standardized holiday menu across all facilities. Rather, some have more flexibility with their menus than others.

Holiday meals “reflect available food items, local considerations, and the cultural diversity of the inmate population,” a spokesperson told Oxygen. “This allows institutions to incorporate menu enhancements and provide meals that recognize the specific holiday.”

The statement added, “The same goes for any planned activities at each facility.”

Though this Thanksgiving marks Combs’ third behind bars, it’s his first at FCI Allenwood Low, where he was transferred in October after sustaining a head injury while incarcerated at New Jersey's FCI Fort Dix.

"His transfer from one low-security facility to another is an important distinction, and while we cannot speak to the BOP's specific reasons for the move, it is consistent with a decision made with safety and security in mind,” Combs’ rep told E! in an Oct. 16 statement. "We are grateful for the attention being given to his well-being and hope he can continue serving his time without unnecessary disruption."

Keep reading to see how more stars are celebrating Thanksgiving 2026…

The “Honey Bee” singer and “Hollaback Girl” hitmaker snuggled in close as they expressed gratitude for their fans. As Shelton wrote on Instagram Nov. 26, “Hoping everybody has a happy Thanksgiving!!! Thankful for y'all!!!!”

The supermodel and jiu jitsu instructor showed off their model life with their 21-month-old son.

“The amount of goodness we experience in life depends on our ability to notice it," Bündchen captioned her Nov. 26 Instagram post, which also featured pictures of her and ex-husband Tom Brady's kids Benjamin, 16, and Vivian, 13. "Gratitude is contagious, and the more we can appreciate the beauty around us, the more joy we bring into our lives and the lives of others."

She added, "May we always find something to be grateful for, not just today, but every day. Happy Thanksgiving! Sending you all so much love."

It was a celebration for the girls as Dunham marked her first Thanksgiving as a mom alongside husband Luis Felber.

As she captioned the Nov. 26 Instagram post as the family went on a stroll, "Thankful."

You oughta know how excited the country music star is about the holiday season.

“Time for a little more peace, love and cowboys,” she wrote on Instagram Nov. 26. “Let the holiday shenanigans begin happy Thanksgiving from my family to y’all’s!”

The Freaky Friday star got reflective this Thanksgiving as she shared an image of herself stretching while enjoying an ocean view.

"Going to turn off the noise for a moment," she wrote on Instagram Nov. 26. "To all out there in this vast environment that we opt into, that if you're lucky enough to have one, the Thanksgiving meal is not hard. It's a roasted bird and potatoes."

"What's hard are the people with their binary and rigid ideas and judgments and petty selfishness," she added. "Today let's all be like Dolly [Parton] and be welcoming and gentle and generous."

The Red Table Talk host showed off her family's extravagant Thanksgiving set-up.

"Preparing for Thanksgiving dinner at the family abode," she wrote on Instagram Nov. 26. "Happy Day of thanks to you all and may you, your families and loved ones continue to be lifted and showered by the gifts of grace from the Highest. They may not always show up how we want them to … but they are there."

#781. DWTS Cohost Julianne Hough Addresses Criticism of Season 35 Fashion

Dancing With the Stars cohost Julianne Hough reacted to fans criticizing her style choices on season 35: “When you get into your late 30s, you just don’t give a f--k anymore.”

Julianne Hough is spinning away from the negativity.

After the Dancing With the Stars cohost made waves for her fashion choices during season 35, she shed insight into her looks while responding to those who gave a low score on her style.

“I really feel like I’m at this next inflection of my career,” Hough told Glamour in an interview published Nov. 24 alongside her stylist Brad Goreski. “When you get into your late 30s, you just don’t give a f--k anymore. You’re like, ‘Who am I? What do I want to wear? What makes me feel incredible?’ It has more intention rather than trying to fit into what’s hot.”

“I feel like I’m in my leading lady era,” she continued. “I mean that in the actual projects that I’m doing, but also me as a person.”

To cohost this season of DWTS alongside Alfonso Ribeiro, the professional dancer decided to take a step out of her usual style comfort zone.

“I’ve gone a little bit more vixen-y this year than I have girl next door because we’re trying to find that character,” she shared. “It’s been very strategic.”

As she twirled with a new vibe, Hough took some fashion risks, including a sultry Valentino ensemble—which featured a skin-colored bodysuit under a see-through skirt—during the Nov. 17 episode that really had fans talking, with one social media user calling for Hough’s stylist to be “fired” in a viral Instagram video.

But as for Goreski, he doesn’t believe the online chatter about Hough’s looks is completely pointe-less anyway, emphasizing that “any conversation, good or bad, around fashion is great.”

“I think Jules ultimately brings the looks to life,” he added, praising his client. “I’m glad that there’s another part of the show that people talk about. Not every person’s going to love every look. I know that from being a stylist for 15 years. And that’s okay.”

And ultimately, Hough concluded that taking those fashion risks is worth it, despite what people may say.

“Apathy is the enemy,” she said, sharing the phrase became her motto for the season. “The reason things exist and have charge and stay visible [is] people either love it or hate it. They still want to talk about it.”

As Hough and DWTS wrap up another season, read on for a deep dive into the reality TV series…

How Much Do the Celebrities Get Paid to Be on Dancing With the Stars?

Citing multiple sources, Variety reported in 2019 that Dancing With the Stars contestants make $125,000 for the rehearsal period and first two weeks of the show. If they progress beyond that point, the outlet continued, they earn more money each week. At the time, sources told the publication stars could earn a maximum of $295,000.

However, Bobby Bones said he made more than this when he won season 27 with Sharna Burgess in 2018.

"That show pays OK," the radio personality said on a Sept. 2025 episode of Jason Tartick's podcast Trading Secrets. "Like, first episode, no money. Second episode, $10,000. I think it's like, $10,000, $10,000, $20,000, $20,000. It ends up being $50,000 an episode if you last."

Also receiving a base salary of around $110,000, Bones continued, "I ended up making close to $400,000 from that show."

ABC has not publicly confirmed any of these figures.

What Do the Pros Get Paid on Dancing With the Stars?

Similarly, little has been shared publicly about how much the pros get paid. But as with the contestants, it seems like the longer they're on the show, the more money they can make.

But even if a pro is eliminated in the first round, they're not leaving the ballroom empty-handed.

"You're guaranteed until a certain amount of weeks," Jenna Johnson said on a June 2025 episode of Kelly Stafford and Hank Winchester's podcast The Morning After. "I think there's different contracts though. I can't speak for everybody."

Do Pros Get Paid More If They Win Dancing With the Stars?

While Johnson—who won season 26 with Olympic figure skater Adam Rippon, as well as season 33 with The Bachelor's Joey Graziadei—says the pros don't get a larger paycheck if they take home what is now called the Len Goodman Mirrorball Trophy, she noted there's still an incentive to make it to the finale (besides bragging rights, of course).

"If you make it all the way to the end, you're getting paid the whole season, which is amazing, and you get a bonus on top of that for making it to the finale," she explained on The Morning After. "If you win, it's not like you win a $1 million and split it with your partner. You're just getting a cute trophy together."

Do the Troupe Members Get Paid as Much as the Pros on Dancing With the Stars?

On a 2022 episode of Trading Secrets, Lindsay Arnold recalled how her salary was cut "more than in half" when she was demoted from pro to troupe member.

How Are Pros and Celebrities Paired Together on Dancing With the Stars?

The pros get little input when it comes to being matched with a celebrity.

"You get no say," Lindsay said on a May 2025 episode of Maggie Sellers' Hot Smart Rich podcast. "It's very much just, 'Here's your partner. Make it work.'"

In fact, Jenna said the pairing is often a secret until the last minute.

"They really want to keep it a secret until you meet them live," Jenna said on The Morning After. "They want that genuine reaction. So I think people always think we know who we have and we're keeping it a secret. Absolutely not. They do not tell us. They really don't even want us to know the cast. It gets leaked a lot, but they want it very hush-hush until you walk in and meet your partner."

As for what the Dancing With the Stars team looks for when making these matches?

"It's based on height, build and personality and compatibility," former showrunner Rob Wade told E! News in 2015. "We don't pair people who aren't going to get on. It's too intense. It's not like The Bachelor or something, we couldn't do that. That would just be miserable experience for the celebrity, for us and the viewer. You don't want to see two people who don't like each other and, quite frankly, we have made that mistake pairing people up who didn't get on so well."

How Often Do the Pros and Celebrities Practice on Dancing With the Stars?

Put simply, a lot."Every day we have four-hour rehearsals," Rylee Arnold, who was partnered with Olympic gymnast Stephen Nedoroscik on season 33, shared on a September 2024 episode of the Lightweights Podcast With Joe Vulpis. "It’s either 9:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m., 1:00 p.m. to 5:00 p.m. or 5:00 p.m to 9:00 p.m."But the work doesn't stop once the rehearsal wraps. Rylee noted she might then meet with producers or the creative team, work on choreography or study dance videos."Literally my whole life is devoted to it," she continued, "but it's my passion and it's what I love. So, it makes me so happy."Indeed, it's a no-days-off kind of gig."We have our show day on Tuesday and then it's Wednesday to Sunday, straight rehearsals," Rylee added. "And then Monday we have camera blocking and then Tuesday's show day again."

Do the Pros Get to Pick the Songs Each Week for Their Dance With Their Celebrity Partner?

"Mostly yes," Emma Slater and Britt Stewart revealed in a September 2025 Instagram video, "though it's a collaboration with producers."

What's the Process Like for Making the Costumes for Dancing With the Stars?

If you thought the quickstep was fast, just wait until you hear about the pace of the costume department."We meet with the set and lighting designers, dancers and talent and create a story [for each pair]," costume designer Daniela Gschwendtner told TV Insider back in 2017. "Then we sketch out ideas. We have five days, max, to make all the outfits. That’s half a day per costume, not including all the rhinestones. The fitting and trimming we do later. We have about 20 people in our department and then we have a separate tailor shop. It’s a big enterprise."In fact, costume designer Steven Norman Lee said pairs usually try on their costumes for the first time just hours before showtime. And while the department "might use a pair of pants again for the boys," he continued, everything is generally made custom each week.As Gschwendtner added, "We do reuse things for group numbers or promo shoots, but not for the competition. We don’t reuse things unless there’s a specific reason to do so. We try to keep everybody fresh and new in something different every week, so it stays interesting."

#779. 'I persuaded my club to give me a job as a content creator'

Making videos with fans and players at his local football club is all in a day's work for Jacob.

He's a content creator for Bolton Wanderers FC, he comes up with new ideas for social media, filming videos and posts them onto official pages. The aim is to encourage people to follow the club.

There are many different ways to develop a career in football content creation, from apprenticeships to freelance work and full-time employment. It isn't just about making videos - content creators need to understanding their audience, respond to analytics and adapt material for different platforms

Jacob works as a content creator for Bolton Wanderers and his career progression has followed this path:

Voluntary work at Bolton --> Professional content creator

While it might look simple, he's had to be resilient - and one of the biggest obstacles he faced was convincing Bolton to create his role. "Don't wait for an opportunity to come to you," he says. "If you're good at it, it does then sometimes lead into getting a role. If it doesn't, you've created a portfolio and it's really good for your CV and future opportunities."

Jacob says salaries can range from Â£26,000 to around Â£40,000 for roles like his. Like him, some content creators start by doing it as a hobby while they improve their skills. While some content creators are full-time employees, many are freelancers so their average salaries can be variable.

Find out more about the role of a content creator below. Content creation roles can come under a range of titles including social media manager or content manager.

You could get into this role via a college course (to get practical skills in video editing and production, or a T Level in Marketing), an apprenticeship, volunteering, short private training courses and also teaching yourself.

This information is a guide and is constantly changing. Please check the National Careers Service website for the latest information and all the qualifications needed and the GOV.UK website for more on T-levels.

#778. How to become a football referee

Honestly, for me it's one of the most rewarding things I've probably ever done. You find so much more out about yourself that you probably never knew.

Louise Thompson, women's referee pathway officer for the Irish Football Association, international FIFA referee, and PremierLeague referee in Northern Ireland.

What does a women's referee pathway officer do?

Looking after female referees within Northern Ireland, trying to recruit, retain and give them experience within their games to pushthrough into top level refereeing.

What kind of training do you give to aspiring referees?

So from going through recruitment courses first of all, and then we do the beginners course with referees, just giving them all of the Laws of the Game knowledge, then we will also do a practical part of that course where they go onto the pitch and we'll go through scenarios, positioning, things around free kick management for example, other set pieces likecorners, penalty setup, what you do as a referee day to day, even pre match stuff as well, so when you arrive at the grounds, how you check the pitch, check all the equipment is there, how you would interact with players, coaches and then just again, maybe createlike a role play sort of environment so that they know that they're not going totally blind into that sort of situation.

Have you always been passionate about football?

Football was a passion of mine, even when I was younger, primary school age, we just didn't have very many female teams, so it normally meant playing with the boys and the boys teams and stuff up until I was about 14, which was the minimum age here you can join senior ladies football team, which is what I did, and played there for 14 years at a club here locally, including up until the Women's Premiership, so it was great to be involved in football, but I always loved watching football, playing football, anything to do with football, I was always there and interested.

How did you go from playing football to being a referee?

Becoming a referee for me sort of happened by chance to be honest. It was during a game, one time I got an injury, quite a bad injury to my knee and then I had seen luckily that the referee course was being advertised. So I signed up for it, but I also signed up for a coaching course pretty much at the same time, maybe about six weeks apart. I wasnât really sure which role I wanted to follow, but over that winter I had been pushed into refereeing a wee bit and said sure, why not, Iâll give it a go, it'd be a bit of extra fitness before my season restarts, and then just fell in love with it from there and never looked back.

What subjects did you study at school and university?

Coming through school I always picked PE, so I did my GCSE PE and then I also did A-level PE and then when I went onto university,I had the sport and exercise science as well within that, so I think it gives you a good understanding of obviously how your body works, and your plan and training, stuff like that as well so you know when you're working nutrition wise, things that you need to know,especially as you reach the top level, just to make sure that you're getting the most out of your body.

What are your top tips for becoming a referee?

I would say definitely give it a try for sure. You never know until you do it. I think even when I was a player, I probably never imaginedthat I would be a referee and that I would even achieve and have experienced what Iâve been able to experience. So you never knowuntil you give it a go, but it's also about probably pushing yourself out of your comfort zone, being comfortable with being uncomfortable in situations like that. It's maybe not always as bad as it probably seems it's going to be. There's probably a lot more stigma around being a referee - who wants to be a referee? - but honestly for me, it's one of the most rewarding things I've probably ever done.

With a lifelong love of football, Louise Thompson followed her passion for the game, first as a player and now as a referee. As well as refereeing Fifa and NIFL Premiership matches, she also works for the Irish Football Association as the women's referee pathway officer, recruiting and developing up-and-coming female refs.

Louise Thompson on refereeing the Women's Irish Cup final.

If you're interested in becoming a referee, it's something you can get involved with from a young age through local referee courses. The minimum age to become a qualified referee varies depending on where in the UK you live:

In her role as a women's referee pathway officer, Louise oversees new referees right from the initial recruitment courses stage: "We then do the beginners' course with referees, giving them all of the Laws of the Game knowledge," she says. "We also do a hands-on part of that course where they go onto the pitch and we go through different scenariosâ¦ exactly what you do as a referee, and day-to-day practical stuff as wellâ¦ The idea is to give them all the basics and fundamentals before they go into a game so that they're prepared."

All four UK nations have established pathways for referee development and progression. Starting out at grassroots level, it's possible to progress all the way to Fifa!

Louise's first games were youth games: "I still remember my first game to this day," she says. "It was an under-13 game, and I was definitely the most nervous person on the pitch." She explains: "Over time, you'll get mentors who will come and watch you, give you advice, give you feedback" which will help you to progress to higher levels of the game.

As well as PE, Louise has found that languages are really helpful in this line of work, "especially when you're dealing with a lot of international games and people coming along," she says. "If you can learn some languages, it's very, very useful."

You could get into this role by training with a professional body.

Sources: National Careers Service, GOV.UK, FA, IFA, SFA, and FAW.

#777. Better educated than ever — yet Germany's Gen Z is being shut out of its own future

Never before have young people around the world been so well-educated while facing so many economic challenges. Young Germans are asking: Will I be better off than my parents?

It is becoming increasingly difficult for young people in Germany to find a job after finishing university or professional training. And finding an affordable place to live in a big city, and finally starting to live independently is becoming almost impossible.

Furthermore, young people do not feel that politicians are taking action on issues that matter to them, such as climate protection. The climate conference in Antalya, Turkey, is a case in point. It, therefore, shouldn't be a surprise that young people across Europe once again took to the streets this Friday, which was World Children's Day too, to make their voices heard. In Germany, Gen Z protests took place in 73 towns and cities.

What particularly infuriates many young people is being talked about rather than spoken to. Equally infuriating is seeing their protests branded as criminal before they have even begun, all because of the actions of a small minority.

One example of such rhetoric was when the youth wing of the conservative Christian Democratic Union/Christian Social Union (CDU/CSU) party in Berlin-Mitte suggested deploying the German army against demonstrations.

It can also be seen in the media, such as when Bild, Germany's highest-circulation tabloid, ran a headline that translated as: "Young, male, known to the police — who rioted after the demonstrations and where chaos threatens today."

"Young people are taking to the streets because they feel they are not being heard. And, of course, that feeling is strongly reinforced when the press devotes no more than a brief paragraph to their demands while focusing the rest of its coverage on how these protests could become problematic," says Erik Sczygiol, who until recently was deputy secretary-general of the Federal Conference of Student Representatives. "Of course, any potential security concerns need to be addressed, but they should not overshadow media coverage of the protests."

The 18-year-old Sczygiol is almost an exception. He was invited to participate in the launch of the World Population Report in Bonn alongside representatives of the United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA) and the German Foundation for World Population (DSW). This year's report, entitled "Succeeding Generations: Empowering young people to chart the future," is particularly noteworthy because it focuses on Gen Z.

UN researchers surveyed 109,000 people across 73 countries for the report, some of whose findings are encouraging. Young people worldwide are better educated than any generation before them, with 78% of adolescents across the globe completing at least lower secondary education. But finding a job is becoming increasingly difficult, while informal employment is on the rise.

This economic uncertainty has far-reaching consequences for young people. According to the report, people often do not achieve financial independence until they are in their mid-to-late 20s, and a stable partnership and parenthood are often not realities before their early-to-mid 30s.

Nor do young people have a seat at the political decision-making table when it comes to shaping future reforms in the labor market, housing or climate protection. Florian Brod, 25, points out: "Almost half of the world's population is under 30, yet only 2.6% of parliamentarians worldwide are under 30."

Young people need and want change to protect their livelihoods and those of future generations. "Yet those who will have to live longest with the consequences of today's decisions are precisely the ones who have hardly any representation in the political decision-making process," says Brod.

He is somewhat close to the political decision-making process as he has served as a Youth Delegate for Sustainable Development for almost two years. In this role, he represents the interests of young people in Germany at United Nations conferences. This is certainly an important step towards giving his generation a greater say in political processes.

Nevertheless, both Brod and Sczygiol have had similar experiences. They often participate in conferences and panel discussions and are invited to submit their opinions, but these invitations often amount to little more than symbolic gestures.

"Having access to an international conference is a first step. But without substantive briefings ahead of the conference, without involvement in preliminary negotiations and, in some cases, without access to negotiation texts, there is little opportunity for us to help shape the outcome. When young people see their demands making little headway politically while they are simultaneously excluded from the search for solutions, frustration inevitably builds," says Brod.

Sczygiol adds: "We often get the feeling at the Federal Youth Conference that we were invited simply to provide a nice photo opportunity. We may be sitting at the table, but often only once a bill has already gone through 17 different drafts and is just days away from its final vote in the Bundestag. By that stage, young people have virtually no say in changing anything, and their voices are barely heard. Their contributions are often simply dismissed with: 'Well, that's just typical youthful nonsense.' And that is something that really frustrates young people."

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Medical student Amelie Belosevic knows that feeling all too well. She served as Germany's Youth Delegate at the World Health Assembly in Geneva in May. Twenty-five countries sent youth representatives, which Belosevic sees as a clear step forward. However, she has one criticism. According to the United Nations Population Fund, 90% of the world's 1.8 billion young people live in the Global South. Yet, the region was represented by only eight delegates. As a result, Africa, Latin America and large parts of Asia were left virtually voiceless.

Her demands for Germany include better job prospects for young people entering the workforce and sustainable pension systems 40 years from now. "For a very long time, people have said 'I believe my children will have a better life than I do.' But that is no longer necessarily true. So it makes sense then that those who feel the greatest anxiety about the future are the people who have most of their life ahead of them. Sometimes, people don't understand that. We young people need to be able to believe in our future again!"

This article was originally published in German.

#776. Orangutans face bleak future after Indonesia’s devastating wildfires

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

An orangutan affected by smoke inhalation receives emergency oxygen.Credit: REUTERS/Willy Kurniawan

For most of October, parts of Indonesia felt dystopian as wildfires turned the sky a reddish orange.

“It felt like you were on Mars,” says Erin Vogel, a primatologist at Rutgers University in New Brunswick, New Jersey.

Vogel was visiting the Tuanan Orangutan Research Station in Central Kalimantan, Indonesia, at the time. She and her colleagues have been conducting research on the critically endangered Bornean orangutan (Pongo pygmaeus) there for more than 20 years, but this trip she spent much of her time fighting fires. There were roughly 300,000 blazes in the region between July and October, and October’s level of toxic particulate matter in the air was roughly 400 times higher than what the World Health Organization deems safe.

Indonesia is experiencing one of its most severe fire and haze season of the past three decades, in part because a super El Niño has dried out vegetation and brought winds that fuelled the flames. More than 2.8 million hectares have burnt across Indonesia so far, and Kalimantan has been affected the worst. Fires devoured 60% of Bornean orangutans’ habitats in Kalimantan, including healthy forests such as those at the Tuanan research station and in Gunung Palung National Park.

Nature spoke to Vogel about the disaster and what it means for orangutans. At the time of the interview, fires were still smouldering in Tuanan peat swamp forests.

It was depressing and horrid. I’ve never seen so much forest loss in the 23 years I have worked in Indonesia. In the sky, there was this orange-brown haze that was very thick and it burnt your lungs if you weren’t wearing a respirator.

When I arrived in Tuanan, it really struck me how quiet the forests had become. You didn’t hear birds; you didn’t hear insects; you didn’t hear anything except trees burning and falling.

The forest staff, the orangutan staff, the phenology staff and the fire teams were all fighting fires. I felt in awe of those heroes voluntarily fighting these fires day and night. They’d all been doing so for more than two months straight. It takes real strength to be able to do that and not give up, and our team is just so positive and hopeful.

We saw some orangutans who seemed to be very lethargic and sick. We came across one of the males we’ve been studying for more than 15 years, and he was on the ground, breathing heavily. But when we saw him a couple of days later, he seemed to have recovered a little bit. He was near the research station, eating some vegetation on the ground, climbing trees and eating fruits. That reassures us that he is doing better.

We’re seeing orangutans being displaced from one area to others. That means we’re going to have competition between individuals over limited resources. That’s also going to change their behaviour. It’s going to be interesting to see what happens.

#775. 'My job combines my passion for gaming and football'

Working on one of the world's biggest football video games is the perfect combination of my two biggest passions, gaming and football.

I'm CJ Ramson. I work on the creation of football video games. I work on Football Manager as an associate QA manager. QA stands for quality assurance.

We're the ones that test the game. We make sure everything works, and we work closely with the developers to try and make the most realistic simulation of football.

Growing up, I loved football, whether that was playing football or playing football video games with my friends. I'd always be doing one or the other. With the video games, the thing that really drew me to them was I've always been into the tactical side of the game, either being able to control the players or create your own tactics.

So a typical day for us, we'll get a new build in from the developers. We'll test it as a QA team, and we'll look for either bugsor ways that we can improve the game. That can be anything from the runs that players make, to decisions they make on the ball, what the team instructions and tactics do. So there's a lot of areas for us to cover. Our final goal is to make it as realistic to real football as possible.

So even though my background was in coaching, there was a lot of transferable skills that I learned and developed through my time coaching that I managed to transfer into this. So whether that's being really analytical and having a good eye for detail and knowingwhen to pick things out and what to look for, or it could be things like timekeeping and making sure things run perfectly on time, and working with other people as well. So social skills where you have to work within a team or even lead a team.

The animation he makes, and the ball physics as well, where the ball goes off after the save."

So as much as I loved playing football, I realised quite early on I probably wasn't going to be a professionalfootballer. But I wanted to work in football and find. So at college, I studied sports science, and that's where I found my love of coaching. I did my FA Level 1 and then went on to do my FA Level 2. After I left college, I got a job at Arsenal, which was unpaid, working with them, learning how to develop my coaching skills. Which then led to me having a full-time paid job at Fulham Football Club, working with the youth teams, working with the academy teams. And then that eventually led to me going to an event. I saw an opportunity where you could apply for a job in Football Manager. It was something that naturally I was interested in, had a conversation with them, and realised it was definitely something that I would love to do.

So I went to the networking event at Kick It Out, and that was an opportunity for me to network with other football coaches, other people within the gaming industries, and have a really good insight to different jobs in football gaming. Without doing that, I wouldn't have the opportunity to meet the people at Football Manager and see a new job in gaming, which I wouldn't have beenaware of.

One of the highlights of my career so far is working on the in-and-out-of-possession system on FM 26. This is something we see in real football all the time, so being part of the team that brought that to life and brought it into the game was super cool.

Working within the football industry is a dream come true. Being able to work on something that I'm passionate about, that is played and enjoyed by millions of people, is an amazing feeling for me and an amazing opportunity that I have. And yeah, I love it.

There are different roles in video game testing. CJ notes that: "Salaries can vary depending on your role and the company you work for. They can range from around Â£20,000 to Â£50,000 and upwards." The higher salaries in this range could apply when you've gained more experienced and progressed in your career.

CJ is now a quality assurance manager, but he started out as a quality assurance tester. Find out more about the role of QA tester below. This role can have various other job titles, such as games tester, computer games tester, and video games tester.

You could get into this role via a university course, a college course (such as a Level 3 Diploma in Creative Media, an A-level in Computing, or a T-level in Digital Software Development (England only)), an apprenticeship, or applying directly if you have relevant experience.

#772. Paige DeSorbo Goes Social Media Official With Boyfriend Joe D’Amelio

Paige DeSorbo debuted her romance with boyfriend Joe D'Amelio on TikTok Nov. 25 nearly two years after the couple first sparked romance rumors.

Paige DeSorbo is serving up a hard launch.

Four months after the Summer House alum denied rumors that she and boyfriend Joe D’Amelio got engaged, she made their romance social media official, sharing a funny video on TikTok of her friends making homemade pizzas.

As DeSorbo captioned the Nov. 25 TikTok video, which she also shared on her Instagram Stories, “We aren’t Italian at all.”

The clip featured the Giggly Squad podcast host’s pals cooking up pies and hanging out as they lip-synced to audio from a scene from the 1990 classic Goodfellas, in which Henry Hill (Ray Liotta) introduces the members of mafia capo Paulie Cicero’s crew.

“There was Jimmy, and Tommy, and me. And there was Anthony Stabile, Frankie Carbone,” Liotta’s Hill says in the scene. “And then there was Mo Black’s brother, Fat Andy and his guys, Frankie the Wop and Freddy No Nose. And then there was Pete the Killer, who was Sally Balls’ brother. Then you had Nickey Eyes and Mikey Franzese.”

And among the family and friends who made a cameo in DeSorbo’s video was D’Amelio, who lifted up his drink in greeting as the camera panned to him during the “Nickey Eyes” line.

While the couple first sparked romance rumors way back in February 2025, they have kept their relationship offline until now. And fans couldn’t help but get excited about the update.

Although this marks the D’Amelio’s debut on DeSorbo’s social media, the Bravo alum previously shared insight into their romance, joking to Us Weekly in a February interview that while Italian men have a reputation for being “not quiet,” she’s found that’s not the case.

The ”We Don’t Talk Anymore” singer announced in October 2022 he was dating someone on The Howard Stern Show, revealing he was “definitely” in love. However, it was not until one month later in December when he shared who that special someone was in an Instagram post.

Puth posted a picture with the College of Charleston alum for his 31st birthday. “Ohhhhh I’m NOT a loser… ‘cause I didn’t lose her!!!”, he wrote under the pictures of the duo kissing in a photobooth. “(Happy birthday to me.)”

The duo went on to tie the knot in September 2024.

#771. Which Premier League players are set for yellow card suspensions?

Yeremy Pino is the latest Premier League player to receive a yellow-card suspension

Crystal Palace's Yeremy Pino has become the latest Premier League player to receive a yellow card suspension after accumulating five bookings since the 2026-27 season began.

Hull City's Matt Crooks and Aston Villa's Matty Cash were the first players to receive a ban for collecting five yellow cards before gameweek 19.

Players receive a one-match suspension if they pick up five or more yellow cards prior to the conclusion of their team's 19th league match of the season.

There are now 17 players sitting on four bookings after 11 rounds of matches, meaning they must avoid another yellow card prior to the halfway point of the season to avoid a ban.

Bournemouth have the most players on the brink of a ban, with three players one yellow card away from suspension.

After that date, the threshold increases to 10 yellow cards. Any player reaching that number before the end of their club's 32nd league match of the season will receive a two-match suspension.

From that point, there are further thresholds at 15 and 20 yellow cards.

For players reaching 15 cautions, they incur a three-match suspension. Punishments for players reaching 20 yellow cards are determined by a regulatory commission.

Those cut-offs do not reset until the end of the Premier League season.

In the Championship, League One and League Two, there are similar thresholds.

However, with those three divisions having 46 rounds of league matches instead of 38, players have to avoid getting 10 yellow cards before the end of the 37th league match in order to not receive a two-match suspension.

In those divisions, the yellow cards are reset at the end of the league season and do not include matches in the play-offs.

The following players have received a one-match ban and will now receive a two-match ban if they reach ten bookings before game week 32:

Yeremy Pino - Crystal Palace (five yellow cards)

Matt Crooks - Hull City (five yellow cards)

If any of the following players receive another Premier League yellow card before the season's halfway point, they will be banned for one match:

Pascal Gross - Brighton & Hove Albion (four)

Oliver Boscagli - Brighton & Hove Albion (four)

Chema Andres - Brighton & Hove Albion (four)

The following players will miss their club's next set of fixtures:

Yeremy Pino - Crytsal Palce (yellow card suspension)

Jean-Philippe Mateta - Crystal Palace (red card suspension)

Igor Thiago - Brentford (red card suspension)

Costinha - Brighton & Hove Albion (red card suspension)

Leny Yoro - Manchester United (red card suspension)

James Tarkowski - Everton (red card suspension)

#770. When is the Nations League quarter-final draw?

England are a seeded side for the Nations League quarter-finals after topping their group

The draw for the final eight teams in the 2026-27 Nations League will be on Friday, 20 November at 11:00 GMT.

It will take place at Uefa's headquarters in Nyon, Switzerland and be broadcast on Uefa TV.

England are the only home nation to have made it to the quarter-final stage, however Northern Ireland's draw against Hungary saw them top Group B2 and secure promotion to League A in the 2028-29 tournament.

Scotland will remain in League B following their third-place finish in Group B1, and Wales face a League A/B relegation play-off in March after being consigned to last place in Group A4.

The Republic of Ireland finished second in Group B3 and so will take part in a League A/B promotion play-off in March.

The winners of groups A1-A4 are seeded for the draw, playing the runners-up of other groups in League A.

England have sealed their place in the last eight as Group A3 winners and could face:

They cannot face A3 runners-up Spain as teams must be drawn against sides from other groups.

The quarter-finals will be played over two legs during the international break between 25-30 March.

Seeded teams get to play the second leg of their quarter-final at home.

Nations that reach the semi-finals can bid those penultimate matches as well as the final.

The remaining dates for the Nations League are:

Semi-finals, third-place play-off and final: 9-13 June

#769. Why Man City can't wear their new kit in Premier League

Manchester City will only be wearing their orange kit for selected Champions League games

Manchester City sported a new orange fourth kit during their Champions League draw with Napoli on Tuesday - but will not be able to wear it in the Premier League.

Top-flight clubs in England can only wear a maximum of three strips in a league campaign, meaning Enzo Maresca's side cannot play in their new kit.

However, there is no limit in the Champions League, meaning City can wear their new strip for the rest of their European campaign.

City can also wear the kit in the FA Cup, provided that an application is made to the Football Association, as well as a reason for its requested use.

That is why Arsenal were allowed to play in a white fourth strip in the 2025-26 FA Cup as part of their campaign to combat youth knife crime in London.

Fans could scan the badge on City's 2025-26 fourth kit to receive items in a video game

City also released a green fourth kit in 2025-26 with a gaming-inspired theme.

The kit, debuted during their Champions League victory over Villarreal, featured an NFC chip in the club badge that fans could scan to unlock gaming rewards.

The club released another fourth kit in the 2024-25 season co-designed by Noel Gallagher in tribute to the 30th anniversary of Oasis' 1994 album 'Definitely Maybe'.

It was worn in the Champions League by the men's team against Inter Milan and Paris St-Germain, and the women's team against Paris FC and Barcelona.

A fifth kit was also used by the men's team during the 2025 Club World Cup

During the 2023-24 season, the women's side also sported a Chinese New Year-inspired shirt in a League Cup victory against rivals Manchester United.

While the Premier League is more restrictive over the number of kits that can be released - the rules are more relaxed in other European leagues.

Napoli wore 13 strips during the 2021-22 season; including a Halloween kit, four different Diego Maradona tributes and four Europa League-specific kits.
